business_problem: BMS needed a shared AI environment that could help scientists reason over huge biological, chemical, imaging, and clinical datasets across global R&D, because isolated compute and manual analysis slowed target discovery, lead optimization, imaging research, and clinical insight generation.
solution_summary: BMS established an AI factory on NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD to unify computational science across target identification, molecular design, imaging, and clinical development. The platform connects research sites and lets scientists shift resources among large language model training, deep learning, imaging, and inference workloads on one hybrid environment managed with Equinix and Mark III Systems. BMS uses the platform to expand its CELMoD compound library, apply its Predict First methodology to lead optimization, and integrate the NVIDIA BioNeMo Agent Toolkit into broader biological and agentic AI workflows. In imaging, teams process CT and MRI data with NVIDIA MONAI and DGX SuperPOD, masking 80–90 percent of scans during self-supervised learning to build foundation models that match human lesion and tumor detection while also quantifying muscle, fat, and bone density. BMS is also applying transformers to clinical-trial data and expanding the environment with a second DGX SuperPOD powered by DGX Vera Rubin NVL72 systems to make the platform globally accessible across R&D.

data_flow: Biological, chemical, imaging, and clinical-trial data flow into the centralized AI factory, DGX SuperPOD resources train or fine-tune models for target identification, molecule design, imaging, and patient-response prediction, and the outputs are fed back into scientist decisions and globally shared R&D programs.
integration_points: research programs in Lawrenceville and San Diego
business_outcome: BMS reports 55 percent overall cost savings versus its prior computing model, weeks of manual work eliminated in target identification, new targets and potential medicines opened through AI-assisted CELMoD expansion, and imaging and clinical models that give scientists higher-conviction signals faster across a globally shared AI platform.
